problems.title: Domain of the shared rational function
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find the domain.
problems.idea: Only the denominator can vanish.
formulas: A rational function is defined where its denominator is nonzero.
steps: The denominator is x-2.
It vanishes only at x=2, and the numerator there is -1, so this is not a removable hole.

problems.title: Area from the three axis intercepts
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find the triangle area formed by its intercepts with the coordinate axes.
problems.idea: Find both x-intercepts and the y-intercept.
steps: The numerator (x-1)(x-3)=0 gives intercepts (1,0),(3,0).
The horizontal base is 2 and perpendicular height is 3/2; area=2·(3/2)/2=3/2.

problems.title: Positive values of the shared rational function
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), solve f(x)>0.
problems.idea: Make a sign chart using zeros and the pole.
steps: The critical values are 1,2,3.
The signs on (-∞,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,∞) are respectively negative,positive,negative,positive.
Exclude zeros because the inequality is strict, and exclude the pole.

problems.title: A derivative at a root
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), calculate f′(3).
problems.idea: Differentiate the divided form.
steps: At x=3, the squared denominator is 1.

problems.title: Increasing on each side of a pole
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find its intervals of increase.
problems.idea: Its derivative is positive, but the domain has two components.
steps: The function strictly increases on (-∞,2).
It also strictly increases on (2,∞).
It is not increasing across the pole: for example f(1)=0 and f(3)=0 despite 1<3.
problems.note: The printed options list this pair twice, once with a union and once with “and.” Both describe the same interval components; the function is not globally monotone across x=2.

problems.title: No minimum across an infinite branch
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find its minimum point.
problems.idea: A positive derivative on each branch gives no interior minimum.
steps: Neither open branch has an endpoint belonging to the domain.
The right branch is unbounded below near 2, so there is no global minimum either.
problems.answer: No local or global minimum point.

problems.title: Second derivative from the divided form
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), calculate f″(1).
problems.idea: Differentiate the reciprocal twice.

problems.title: State curvature by its derivative sign
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), determine its curvature intervals.
problems.idea: A sign statement avoids ambiguity in translated curvature terminology.
formulas: f″=-2/(x-2)³; f″>0 means concave up, f″<0 means concave down.
steps: For x<2, the denominator is negative, so f″>0: the graph bends upward.
For x>2, f″<0: the graph bends downward.
There is no inflection point at x=2 because the function is undefined there.
problems.answer: Concave up on (-∞,2); concave down on (2,∞).
problems.note: The source uses a negative-form curvature term. Both signs and the matching intervals are given explicitly.

problems.title: Every output is reached on a branch
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find the range.
problems.idea: Use the continuous increasing right branch.
formulas: On (2,∞), f is continuous; f→-∞ at 2⁺ and f→∞ at ∞.
steps: By continuity the right branch passes through every real height.
Thus the complete function has all real values.

problems.title: The slant asymptote is the polynomial part
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find its slant asymptote.
problems.idea: The remaining reciprocal tends to zero at both infinities.
formulas: A slant asymptote y=mx+b satisfies f(x)-(mx+b)→0.
steps: This tends to zero as x→±∞.

problems.title: Left-hand behaviour at the pole
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find the limit as x→2⁻.
problems.idea: The reciprocal term dominates.
steps: Set t=x-2; then f=t-1/t.
From the left t is negative and tends to zero. The first term tends to zero and the second to +∞.

problems.title: A rational limit at negative infinity
problems.question: For f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2), find the limit as x→-∞.
problems.idea: The linear term determines the limit.
steps: The expression is x-2-1/(x-2).
The first part tends to -∞ while the reciprocal vanishes.

problems.title: Reverse the chain rule
problems.question: Find $\int x/\sqrt{x^2-3}\,dx$.
problems.idea: The numerator is half the derivative of the radicand.
steps: For u=x²-3, u′=2x.
Therefore d√(x²-3)/dx=x/√(x²-3).
Add an arbitrary constant on each domain interval |x|>√3.

problems.title: An indefinite integral needs its constant
problems.question: Find $F(\pi/6)$ if $F(x)=\int\sin^2x\,dx$.
problems.idea: Keep the integration constant unless an initial value fixes it.
steps: Without a normalization, this is not one numerical value. If F(0)=0 is intended, C=0.
problems.note: The question omits the integration constant. Even with C=0, the printed option (π-3√3)/24 has an incorrect coefficient of π.

problems.title: Integrate the polynomial and reciprocal separately
problems.question: Find the indefinite integral of f(x)=(x²-4x+3)/(x-2)=x-2-1/(x-2).
problems.idea: Polynomial division makes each part standard.
steps: Integrate x-2-1/(x-2) term by term.
The result is (x-2)²/2-ln|x-2|+C, on each side of x=2.
Differentiating recovers the original rational function.
problems.note: The closest printed choice omits the constant and absolute-value signs; it applies only on x>2 as written.

problems.title: A cylinder whose net is a square
problems.question: A cylinder’s lateral net is a square of side a. Find its volume.
problems.idea: The square sides are the cylinder height and circumference.
steps: The radius is a/(2π).
Hence V=π[a/(2π)]²a=a³/(4π).

problems.title: Volumes share the same apex height
problems.question: In pyramid SABC, triangle ABC is right at C and A=60°. CD is its altitude to AB. Find V(SCBD)/V(SCAD).
problems.idea: The two pyramids have equal perpendicular heights, so compare base areas.
steps: Triangles CBD,CAD share altitude CD, so their area ratio is BD/AD.
Since A=60°, BC/AC=tan60°=√3.
Therefore BD/AD=(√3)²=3, also the volume ratio.

problems.title: An equilateral cone section fixes the slant
problems.question: A cone’s base contains an inscribed equilateral triangle of side √6. A section through the vertex and one triangle side is equilateral. Find the cone volume.
problems.idea: The section’s equal sides are cone generators.
steps: The base radius is √6/√3=√2.
The section gives slant L=√6, so h=√(6-2)=2.
The volume is π·2·2/3=4π/3.

problems.title: Both cone walls belong to the rotated surface
problems.question: An isosceles triangle with equal sides 1 and apex angle 120° rotates around one equal side. Find the resulting surface area.
problems.idea: The rotated solid has outer and inner conical walls.
formulas: Cone lateral area=πrL; triangle base=√3 by the cosine rule.
steps: The off-axis vertex is distance r=sin120°=√3/2 from the axis.
The outer generator is the triangle base √3; the inner generator is the other equal side 1.
Both walls are exposed; the axis edge creates no area. Total area=π(√3/2)(√3+1).

problems.title: Scale a regular hexagonal pyramid
problems.question: A regular hexagonal pyramid has lateral edge 1 inclined 60° to the base. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Find the height and hexagon side by projection.
steps: The base area is 3√3/8.

problems.title: Circumradius of a regular tetrahedron
problems.question: A regular tetrahedron has all edges 3. Find its circumsphere radius.
problems.idea: The sphere centre divides a vertex-to-face altitude in ratio 3:1.
steps: The altitude comes from H²=a²-(a/√3)²=2a²/3.
The symmetry centre lies three quarters of the way from the face toward the vertex.
problems.note: None of the printed choices equals this value; the choices appear to have been copied from the preceding question.

problems.title: A tangent parallel to a given line
problems.question: Find the tangent to y=x⁴ parallel to y=32x.
problems.idea: Match the derivative to the required slope.
steps: 4x³=32 gives x=2, with y=16.
The tangent is y-16=32(x-2).

problems.title: Specify the axial section of a square frustum
problems.question: A regular square-pyramid frustum has base sides 2 and 6 and face slant height 5. Find its axial-section area.
problems.idea: A plane through the axis may use base midlines or diagonals.
steps: The vertical height is √21.
A section through midpoints of opposite base sides has parallel sides 2 and 6, hence area 4√21.
A diagonal axial section instead has sides 2√2 and 6√2, hence area 4√42.
problems.answer: $4\sqrt{21}$ for the midpoint section; $4\sqrt{42}$ for the diagonal section.
problems.note: An arbitrary axial plane is not uniquely specified for a square frustum. The listed answer 4√21 uses the section through side midpoints.

problems.title: Use the angle of the unrolled sector
problems.question: A cone has lateral area 10π cm² and unrolled-sector angle 36°. Find the total surface area.
problems.idea: The sector angle gives the radius-to-slant ratio.
steps: From rL=10 and L=10r, obtain 10r²=10, so r²=1.
The base adds π cm² to the lateral 10π cm².

problems.title: A line’s angle with the xz-plane
problems.question: Find the sine of the angle between $(x-3)/1=(y+4)/2=(z-17)/(-2)$ and the xz-plane.
problems.idea: The perpendicular-to-plane component is the y-component.
steps: The line direction is (1,2,-2), with length 3.
The xz-plane unit normal is (0,1,0), giving perpendicular component 2.
Hence sinθ=2/3.
